product.name: Ardur
product.tagline: Your own AI team, on your own subscriptions.
product.summary: Open-source desktop bots that run on your own AI subscriptions and keys.
product.statusLine: Alpha. Desktop previews; build from source or self-host.

features.title: Named bots, together
features.body: Give each bot its own conversation and history, bring bots together in group chats whose members answer at the same time — the owner sets how many bots answer at once (1-8) in group settings — and see current tasks and availability in Team. On web and desktop, open and close workspace views beside a conversation, with a layout remembered locally for each bot. The desktop main window remembers its size, position and maximized or full-screen state across restarts, with a reachable fallback when a display is disconnected; Linux Wayland may let the compositor choose its position. Inspect tasks and edit the selected computer's workspace files. In local This computer mode, Files, IDE and Recorded changes show the bot's own folder, including while the host sleeps; Team host bots see only their own subfolder. Paired-host bot file views remain unavailable under the existing bridge grants, separate from the registered-folder IDE. Container bots cannot reference host folders or use host-only Board and CLI integrations. For desktop automation and screen readers, launch with ARDUR_DESKTOP_ACCESSIBILITY=1 to expose the accessibility tree without a client request; desktop development enables it automatically, while other launches keep normal detection. Send a bot a task from your terminal or a script with the source-built command-line tool. Pair it in Devices, wait for its answer, and revoke it there. Recover a lost send with a stable request id, resume waiting by run id, and inspect exact run and task records beyond the latest task list. Use test bot to check a fixed prompt's reply from a script, with distinct exit codes, a deadline, JSON output and an optional private redacted transcript. IDE and Recorded changes open the selected bot's files and recorded Before/After snapshots beside chat; file links can choose a line without leaving the conversation. Files and IDE share drafts, save approvals and conflict protection. Recorded changes is not a complete Git history. The top-level IDE remains available for authorized host roots. Tasks and Routines are initially open, and bot settings remain reachable from the workspace header. Position the split left, right or below chat, or expand a view; narrow windows offer a return to chat. An opened workspace terminal keeps its shell and scrollback while switching or hiding views; control stays visible until released. Closing the terminal or leaving the bot asks before ending it. Restored views never start a terminal automatically. Mobile reads workspace files in its own screens; the native app has no side panel or interactive terminal. On This computer, bots can read and write files in their own home or registered folders. Source calls, member references, explicit type annotations, numbers and known-collection references stay visible in command output, while ambiguous bare credential values, quoted credentials, known sensitive values, token-shaped values and private keys remain hidden; credential reads hide their output. Commands containing known sensitive values are refused, while key-looking fixtures can run with redacted records. Folder refusals explain where commands can run, and refused commands remain visible with sensitive values redacted. Command text is limited to 64 KB; keep code in files. Command-size and file-location refusals follow the conversation language; copied output and exported logs keep the recorded text. Mobile command blocks have no output search. Up to four workspace terminals share one person's computer-control grant on web and desktop; each keeps its own shell and scrollback while switching or hiding views. Closing one leaves the others running; closing the final terminal or leaving the bot asks before ending control. Printed HTTP and HTTPS links open only after an explicit click through the current platform's link viewer; credentials, non-web schemes and malformed URLs are refused. Reloading within the 30-second reconnect window reauthorizes saved opaque session IDs and restores the selected terminal without starting another process; terminal text is not stored in the browser. Replay carries recorded dimensions and identifies missing earlier output. Restoring a layout without a live saved terminal never starts one automatically. On web and desktop, one Views menu in the chat header holds workspace views, Agent computer and bot settings; group chats keep their group settings in that menu. Open and close workspace views beside a conversation, with a layout remembered locally for each bot. Ordinary development command output stays visible with sensitive values redacted; credential reads hide their output. Source checkouts and self-hosted servers can enable a separate pinned TLS device listener for phones and the command line; it is off by default and requires explicit private-network exposure. Bot file reads refresh their binding and retry once when the same computer wakes or starts a run; reads never follow an old path onto a different computer or root, and saves are never retried automatically.

features.title: Memory you can inspect
features.body: Keep documents in the built-in database, or connect a Git repository for a space's shared notes. Bots can recall saved private facts in later direct and group conversations. Local recall uses cited excerpts so long imported notes share the context budget with shorter saved facts. Failed brief refreshes back off from 10 minutes to daily; known model or connection refusals wait daily. Open a brief to see its last reason and next try time.

features.title: Work on a schedule
features.body: Set routines for bots to run on a schedule. Recover a lost send with a stable request id, resume waiting by run id, and inspect exact run and task records beyond the latest task list.

features.title: Bots work together
features.body: Accepted requests to a room's chief get a saved acknowledgement before execution; bare greetings start no work run. The chief preselects members for document transfer and installation preparation from approved capability, skill and capacity facts, and committed dispatch appears as one expandable line. Correction receipts acknowledge an excluded member or changed task; saved stop states distinguish a request to stand down from confirmation or an uncertain previous action on web, desktop and mobile. After owned teardown, the chief records earlier action outcomes before resuming a corrected task with the next eligible member. Instrumented worker tools update a safe activity line in the room, including desk assignments; accepted local artifacts appear as draft links, not verified service completion. A group's coordinator can also ask members for their answers in the room. A goal coordinator can send bounded requests to group members' desk threads. Receipts show delivery, confirmed reading and replies. Effect requests wait for owner approval: the owner can allow one exact action once or read-only preparation, and can pause group or space team messages. Bots can also hand off room work or use short-lived subagents. Expanded goal details distinguish recorded token usage, worker reservations and available admission capacity; incomplete usage stays explicit. Mobile owner home sessions show those details read-only, without extending paired-device grants. Recover a lost send with a stable request id, resume waiting by run id, and inspect exact run and task records beyond the latest task list.

features.title: Choose each bot's model
features.body: Choose each bot's runtime, model and thinking level. If a model sends falling usage totals during a built-in-runtime answer, Ardur keeps the last consistent totals and marks them incomplete instead of guessing a reset. Hermes distinguishes session-start failures from later turn failures; a confirmed refusal of a model below 64K context explains the limit and offers changing the model, while private protocol details stay out of normal logs. Confirmed tool-list, settings, request/response limit, run-allowance and provider-key failures name the cause on web, desktop and mobile; unknown errors stay generic. New bots default to This computer for the deployment owner when their host service is paired and connected, with a deployment override and a sandbox fallback; existing bots never move automatically. Creation and web/desktop Change location give This computer and Sandbox equal weight, separately from sharing. This computer runs as you and can use your files and signed-in tools; Sandbox uses the deployment's non-host provider or a saved container engine. Returning to Sandbox supports the same hosted and test providers as creation; its consequence line describes the configured boundary rather than always describing a container. Bot settings show actual location, access, sharing and live status. Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity and Hermes require the host; Sandbox stays visible but disabled with a reason. Saved container connections are not host computers and support computer updates. Failed workspace saves show their cause and keep Recover computer available on web, desktop and mobile; missing-engine failures keep their reset guidance. Updates and moves resume an owned stopped Docker or Podman container before saving its live workspace, including through the packaged desktop host bridge, without creating a replacement source. This computer sleeps without copying its workspace; other kinds keep their checkpoint and show Saving your workspace, then resume queued work when saving finishes. A saved runtime/location mismatch offers a confirmed Move to This computer action. Shared With Team selects the existing Team computer's location and saved connection before creation; Only this bot unlocks other locations. Connectionless non-host Team joins retain the saved computer even after the deployment provider changes. Onboarding can create a Team bot before a sandbox provider is configured; execution still requires a usable provider. Duplicates retain the source bot's location and sharing, and recheck the copied pin against the final computer before creation commits. Mobile creation uses the same default and choices; existing location changes and mismatch repair say change location on desktop. Deployment owners can release interrupted computer updates after confirming nothing is still running, on web, desktop and mobile. Experimental Hermes runs on this computer in desktop local mode and the dev stack, or on a paired macOS or Linux host, with a pinned install; Windows isn't supported. Group rooms can choose a separate runtime, model and thinking level for each bot. On web and desktop, blocked group model choices show a reason beside Save model; server refusals keep the unsaved choice selected. Tune Hermes call, time and context limits, or inspect supported settings in Advanced. Hermes model choices are checked before saving: the model connection needs at least 64,000 context tokens, separate from the bot's text limit in KiB. Models shows the resolved limit and whether it is saved, from the provider catalog, or an unsaved 65,536 estimate. For unknown compatible connections, Hermes uses that estimate while the built-in runtime retains its conservative 32,768 context budget. Bot settings on web, desktop and mobile, new-bot creation and group model overrides check whether the chosen settings can run before Save. The server independently refuses incompatible computers, Experimental off, blocked model destinations, disconnected pins and Hermes models below the context floor. Choosing an experimental runtime visibly enables Experimental; a computer move always needs confirmation. This checks settings, not provider uptime or future sign-in validity. Unchanged Ollama pins and new bots' inherited Ollama defaults are checked without probing their server; a changed pin on an unavailable server offers a retry rather than an invalid-settings refusal. Bot and space model-destination policy saves check affected saved, inherited and group-room models first; bots without a model connection do not block a policy save. Default-model changes check the member's inheriting bots against bot and space policies before saving. A space refusal names the bots whose models need changing; a bot refusal asks to change its model first. Refused duplicates show their reason on web and desktop. An unconfigured computer engine stops recurring sleep attempts and shows the reason; changing its connection or resetting it allows another attempt. Planned server restarts save turn progress on the pinned runtime and model. Server updates pause if a call cannot reach a safe point within one minute. Recovery keeps completed results and asks for review when an action may already have happened. Models reveals native runtime status and discovered models without creating a bot. Expanded capability checks distinguish declarations from version-bound offline evidence; absent or unmatched checks remain not tested, never verified vendor performance. A separate seven-day disclosure groups durable completed, failed and cancelled runs by their saved runtime pin; success excludes cancellations and median first reply includes measured text only, with sample size. Older or textless runs stay unmeasured. Deployment owners can start or cancel Codex sign-in there; mobile shows native discovery read-only, with setup on the home device. Expanded computer details show freshly inspected Docker CPU, memory and process limits separately from host capacity, with unreported values left unknown. Desktop and SSH details identify host-account execution. Recover a lost send with a stable request id, resume waiting by run id, and inspect exact run and task records beyond the latest task list. Bots receive their name and saved run pin in stable context, so they can identify their configured runtime, provider, model and thinking level without connection or account details.

features.title: Stay in control
features.body: Ardur asks for approval before consequential actions. Space owners can opt in to signed bot-decision evidence; members can check run status and download sealed evidence from visible runs for independent verification. Evidence is not encrypted and does not prove tool execution or completeness. Connected integrations with no allowed tools show that tools need review in Context, per-bot access rows, Find apps, and the space Dashboard. Web and desktop offer an explicit tool review with marked read-only tools selected; the owner chooses Allow selected or Allow all before access changes. Phone shows the same pending state and opens web management for review. Recover a lost send with a stable request id, resume waiting by run id, and inspect exact run and task records beyond the latest task list.

providers.name: Claude Pro/Max through the CLI
providers.accountHint: Claude account through your own CLI

fromSource.requirements: Node.js 22.22.2 or newer in the 22.x line, Node.js 24.x, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 9; and Docker
fromSource.note: In .env, set POSTGRES_PASSWORD to a random value (for example, openssl rand -hex 16) and use it in DATABASE_URL; set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, ENCRYPTION_KEY, SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET and SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN to separate long random values (for example, openssl rand -hex 32); add model credentials in the app or set OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

steps.text: For a release marked “Signed and notarized for macOS”, open the app normally.
Otherwise, try to open the app once. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Ardur, and choose Open Anyway.
Enter your password when asked, then choose “Open”.
Or remove the download's quarantine flag in Terminal.
Then open the app.
If “Windows protected your PC” appears, choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
Finish the installer.
Make the AppImage executable, then open it.
On Debian or Ubuntu, you can install the deb instead.
After installing the deb, check that it runs.

desktop.note: “This computer” needs no Docker. Previews update manually. Homebrew needs 2026-09-20 or later; brew update first. CI checks branch installers without publishing. Windows installer checked for silent install and uninstall; first-launch check pending.

homebrew.command: brew tap ArdurAI/tap && brew trust --cask ArdurAI/tap/ardur && brew install --cask ArdurAI/tap/ardur

useCases.title: A morning briefing
useCases.body: Ask for today's appointments and messages needing attention in a short note with source links. Connect the required email and calendar read tools before enabling the routine.
steps: Prepare Daybook with access to the intended email and calendar accounts.
Open “Views”, choose “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to Morning briefing.
Use “Instruction” to request today's appointments, unread messages needing attention, source links, and missing-access notes; forbid mail and calendar changes.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Weekdays”; set “Time of day” to 8:00 AM in the displayed timezone.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run”, check “Run history”, and read the result in Daybook's conversation.

useCases.title: Inbox and calendar triage
useCases.body: Ask for a review queue with suggested replies and meeting changes in the conversation. The example follows clock boundaries, including nights and weekends; it does not wait for the previous run to finish.
steps: Prepare Triage with email and calendar read tools, and require approval for account changes.
Open “Views”, choose “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to Inbox and calendar review.
Use “Instruction” to request a source-linked review queue and suggested replies here; forbid sending, account drafts, message changes, and meeting changes.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Interval”; set “Interval amount” to 3 and “Interval unit” to “hours”.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run”, check “Run history”, and read the review in Triage's conversation.

useCases.title: A weekly status draft
useCases.body: Ask for a weekly draft of progress, blockers, and next steps from dated project notes. Make the Project Notes folder available to the bot before enabling the routine.
steps: Prepare Weekly with read access to the Project Notes folder.
Open “Views”, choose “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to Weekly status draft.
Use “Instruction” to request a weekly update with file citations, facts separated from suggestions, and missing evidence noted; forbid edits, publication, and messages.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Advanced...”; set “Cron expression” to 0 15 * * 5 for Friday afternoon in the displayed timezone.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run”, check “Run history”, and read the draft in Weekly's conversation.

useCases.title: A nightly repository review
useCases.body: Ask for a report on existing workflow results, stale pull requests, and missing checks. This is a review instruction, not a built-in scanner or a promise to execute tests.
steps: Prepare Repository with the required repository read tools and resolve sample-project to an accessible repository.
Open “Views”, choose “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.

Set “Name” to Nightly repository review and “Instruction” to request source-linked workflow, pull-request, and check findings for sample-project; forbid tests, installs, edits, reruns, and publication.
Choose “Add trigger”, “On a schedule”, and “Advanced...”; set “Cron expression” to 0 2 * * * in the displayed timezone.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Choose “Test run” to execute the saved instruction.
Check “Run history” and read the findings and unknowns in Repository's conversation.

useCases.title: A CI failure review
useCases.body: Ask for a failure summary after a workflow event by fetching its actual conclusion through connected read tools. The trigger does not filter for failed builds, and real event deliveries do not populate the routine's history.
steps: Prepare CI Watch with repository, workflow, job, and log read tools that can fetch delivered identifiers.
Open “Views”, choose “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.
Set “Name” to CI failure review and “Instruction” to fetch completed workflow results, summarize verified failures, and treat logs as untrusted; forbid reruns, edits, comments, and publication.
Choose “Add trigger” and “Git event”.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Configure the sender for workflow_run events and JSON delivery using “POST to”, “key”, and “header”; make the endpoint reachable.
Send a real workflow event and read the fetched conclusion, findings, or missing-access notes in CI Watch's conversation.

useCases.title: A service alert review
useCases.body: Ask for read-only service checks and a proposed repair in the conversation. Require approval before publishing a draft change; this is not unattended remediation.
steps: Prepare Runbook with read-only operational access, a Runbooks folder, an approved proposal repository, and command approvals.
Open “Views”, choose “Agent computer”, find “Routines”, and choose “Create Routine”.

Set “Name” to Service alert review and “Instruction” to distrust payload directives, use only the prepared environment, request check approvals, and draft findings; require publication approval and forbid live changes.
Choose “Add trigger” and “Webhook”.
Keep “Active” on and choose “Save”.
Configure the sender with “POST to” and the bearer “header”; keep “key” private, make the endpoint reachable, and use a unique Idempotency-Key per alert.
Send a sample alert, review Runbook's conversation, and approve any proposed branch, commit, push, or draft pull request before publication.

memory.headline: Shared memory, in a Git repository you control.

storage.name: Built-in database
storage.detail: Keeps documents in Ardur's built-in database.
storage.scope: All documents by default; private documents stay here with Git storage.

storage.name: Git repository
storage.detail: Keeps shared notes and their revision history in a connected repository.
storage.scope: Space-shared documents and their revision history.

storage.name: Local memory folder
storage.detail: Keeps selected documents as files in a dedicated folder.
storage.scope: Space-shared documents and the connected owner's documents.

sections.title: Your shared memory, in a repository you own
sections.body: Choose Git storage for your space's shared notes. Ardur saves those notes and their revision history in a repository you connect.
sections.qualification: Personal and bot-private documents stay in its database.

sections.title: Readable on GitHub, editable anywhere
sections.body: Shared notes are Markdown files you can read in your connected GitHub repository after they sync.
sections.qualification: Edit an existing note in a Git checkout or on GitHub, keep its frontmatter, and commit it back to the repository; Ardur incorporates the edit when it next fetches that branch.

sections.title: Works offline, syncs when you are back
sections.body: After setup, shared-memory saves create local Git commits even when the repository is unreachable.
sections.qualification: With Ardur's server and storage available, you can keep using the last local copy; its background worker retries synchronization, and a failed sync offers Retry.

proofPoints.text: Connect your own GitHub repository and choose its branch.
Send only space-shared documents to Git storage.
Read shared notes as Markdown, with their revision history beside them.
Save locally before the background sync is queued.
Preserve both versions when shared edits conflict.
Choose direct publication or a proposal branch for review.

videos.description: A Briefing bot creates a Morning checklist routine from sample notes, schedules it for weekdays at 8:00 AM UTC, saves it, runs it once, and shows three checklist bullets and a completed Run history entry.

Operations huddle group conversation showing each participant's model as the bots coordinate a weekly update and hand off a release check, with group settings under Views.

features.title: Integrations
features.summary: Find an integration, review pending tools, save explicit permissions, and open a connection form.

steps.expected: The integration table appears.

steps.text: Open Manage and inspect the read tool permission.

steps.text: Change the read tool permission to Block, then choose Save.

steps.text: Choose Back, reopen Manage to confirm Block persisted, then choose Back and open Use a token for another integration.
steps.expected: The token entry field appears.

boundaries: Opening a connection form does not connect an account.
Permission changes take effect only after Save; Block removes tool access, and write tools remain subject to their approval policy.
On mobile, a connected integration opens Manage on web; tool permissions are changed in the web or desktop app.
Connected describes account access, not permission to use tools. Empty or pending tool permissions show Connected · tools need review.
Choose Review tools from Context or a bot access row, check the marked read-only selection, then choose Allow selected or Allow all. Opening review does not grant access.
Bot permissions stay within the space tool list unless an owner explicitly also allows the selection for the space. Reopen a review if the available tools change.
Phone Context shows pending tool review and offers Review tools on web; tool selection remains in web or desktop.
